item.title: Darien's Ben Rolapp, Boston College commit, quarterbacks Brunswick to brink of undefeated season
item.description: Darien's Ben Rolapp, the two-year starting quarterback for the Brunswick football team, has helped lead the Bruins to a 9-0 record this season. (Dave Stewart/Hearst Connecticut Media) Ben Rolapp was in his first year as Brunswick football's starting quarterback when he squared off against an old friend. Charlie Thom, the target for many of Rolapp's passes while teammates at Darien High, was doing a post-graduate year as a tight end for Avon Old Farms. The result was a cool, not cool moment. "That was cool. Not cool that we lost, but cool seeing him play," Rolapp said with a smile. A little more than a year later, Rolapp and Brunswick fit into the very cool category - unbeaten at 9-0, with a revenge win over Avon Old Farms (without Thom). The Bruins defeated Williston Northampton 29-28 on Saturday to win the Northeast Prep Conference championship, and will host Taft in the Drew Gamere Championship Bowl on Saturday at 1 p.m. at Cosby Field in Greenwich. Rolapp has a verbal commitment to Boston College and is still receiving Division I looks, including an offer from Penn State. Life is certainly good when you're wanted. "Any time I feel stressed about the (recruiting) process, I just remember I worked for this and pressure is a privilege," Rolapp said. "Brunswick has been awesome. I'm still 100% committed to Boston College and at the end of the day, it's amazing to be wanted." Rolapp was already on Division I radars while at Darien High, where he led the Blue Wave to consecutive Class L finals in 2023 and 2024 before transferring to Brunswick before the 2025 season. He had watched Wave teammate Kevin Roche, a 6-foot-9 tight end now at Georgia Tech, go through the recruiting process and learned from the experience. This season, he's leveled up with more than 2,500 passing yards and a 70% completion rate while leading the Bruins to a perfect record thus far. Wayne McGillicuddy, Brunswick's football coach and director of upper school athletics, said what he's seen in Rolapp this season is a player who is now comfortable in the system and is reacting to the speed of the game and the opposition. "It's hard to play quarterback for us. We put a lot on the quarterback's plate," McGillicuddy said. "That's the biggest thing for him, being comfortable within the offense and knowing everything. It's like having a second coach out there." While nine wins is the key number, Rolapp has put up some eye-popping stats across the schedule. He passed for 362 yards and five touchdowns in a 49-21 win over Phillips Andover on Oct. 24, and followed that by passing for 459 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for 80 yards and two more scores in a 34-30 win over Phillips Exeter Academy the next week. Senior Noah Park, a Greenwich resident who will play at Princeton, has become friends with Rolapp, and the pair has developed a terrific connection on the field. item.title: With Dylan Harper out, Spurs turn to familiar face to fill the void
item.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Julian Champagnie (30) hugs teammate Victor Wembanyama (1) as they celebrate a 124-112 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers in an NBA basketball game, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, in San Antonio. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Whether coming off the bench or starting, at home or on the road, a pre-game nap is a must for the Spurs' Julian Champagnie. "If you let me, I'll sleep for four hours," he said. Champagnie typically wakes up from his midday snooze rested and ready to go. That was certainly the case Thursday night when he scored 10 of his 20 points in the fourth quarter on 4-of-6 shooting, a flurry that helped the Spurs capture a 124-112 win over the Los Angeles Clippers before a sellout crowd of 18,532 at the Frost Bank Center. The grind-it-out victory - the Clippers trailed by just two points midway through the fourth after overcoming a 14-point second-quarter deficit - represented a nice bounce back for the Spurs following a loss to Detroit two days earlier that snapped their 12-game winning streak. It also highlighted Champagnie's value as a versatile good soldier. He moved into the starting lineup after the Spurs learned earlier in the day they would be without the dynamic Dylan Harper for two to three weeks following the 20-year-old's diagnosis of a left hip external rotator strain. "He's been doing it for a while for this team," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said, referring to Champagnie's skill at filling whatever role is asked of him. Harper sustained the injury when he slipped on the court late in Tuesday's 105-93 loss to the Pistons while attempting to catch a pass from Stephon Castle. It was a scary moment for the Spurs as they watched their second-leading scorer clutch at his groin as he lay on the court in visible pain. But they let out a big sigh of relief after learning Harper did not suffer a serious injury and could be back on the court as soon as early December. "The visuals and optics of falls, potential injuries, whatever you want to call it, can be impressionable, and that one did not look great," Johnson said. "And so there's a lot of WebMD (searching), and you try to not let your mind run the wrong way. You hope for the best, but you really don't know. And it's part of things we can't control. "So just very lucky, fortunate, and mostly just happy for Dylan. Obviously, there'll be some (recovery) time, but very best-case scenario for a lot of the things that could have been." item.title: PGA Tour pros embrace clearer pathway under 2028 competitive overhaul
item.description: ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. – The PGA Tour's sweeping competitive overhaul , approved Monday by the Tour's board, is being welcomed by players who believe the new structure will create a simpler, more merit-based path to golf's highest level when it launches in 2028. The changes, developed by the Tour's Future Competition Committee, introduce a revamped promotion system centered on a new Challenger Series and expanded opportunities for players to advance based strictly on performance. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp outlined the new structure, but committee member Maverick McNealy perhaps best captured the motivation behind the overhaul. He described the previous system as a patchwork of rules that had evolved over time and said the committee started with a simple objective: build a format that is fair, competitive and easy to understand. "It was a really kind of tangled, convoluted system that had evolved over time, little tweaks here and there," McNealy said. At the center of the changes is a more clearly defined pathway to the PGA Tour's highest level. McNealy believes the new structure addresses a longstanding problem for players with limited status, who often spend much of a season waiting to learn when and where they will compete. Under the current system, players without full status can find themselves chasing opportunities, entering events that may not fit their schedules and competing against players with access to the Tour's biggest tournaments. “Those guys don't know when they're going to play,” McNealy said. “There's a lot of guys that get caught in that churn that don't have the opportunity to separate themselves against their peers. I think that's going to be a really compelling part of the Challenger Series is how clear-cut the competition is.” The new model also expands opportunities for Korn Ferry Tour members, with 10 players earning promotion to the Championship Series. McNealy expects that change to make the 2028 Korn Ferry Tour season one of the most competitive in the circuit's history. “I think we're going to have the most compelling season on the Korn Ferry Tour in history because 10 players from the Korn Ferry Tour are going to the Championship Series, which is a huge opportunity for those guys,” he said. He believes the system will be most effective because advancement is based strictly on performance. “Frankly, if you start deciding where people go, people get upset, but if you tell everyone to play for it, this is the number you've got to get to, whoever plays the best wins,” McNealy said. “So the more meritocratic system we can have, the more excited everyone's going to be about it.” Not everyone is ready to declare the changes a success, but early reaction from players was generally positive. item.title: Penn State vs. Rutgers: Two Keys to Victory
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Penn State vs. Rutgers should be a blowout with the three-score favorites, the Nittany Lions, winning their final home game of the season, but this is college football. This sport, the birthplace of which lies in New Brunswick, N.J., is famous for producing upsets of epic proportions annually. Penn State will try to avoid being a victim of one of those headline moments. Here are two ways the Nittany Lions can do that and advance to 7-4 on the year. Penn State vs. Rutgers: Two Keys to Victory Sacks, Sacks and More Sacks If there’s a game for Penn State’s defense to dominate the line of scrimmage, it’s this game against Rutgers. The pass rush has been an issue all year, ranking 114th nationally with 14 sacks, but the group stood out last week against Minnesota with a season-high three sacks. Penn State fared well against a stationary quarterback like Drake Lindsey and should fare just as well, if not better, against projected Rutgers starter AJ Surace . Surace has been sacked a whopping 18 times this season as the Scarlet Knights’ backup behind an offensive line that has allowed 27 sacks all season (122nd in FBS). Surace also has 35 carries for -65 yards (counting sack yards), and his longest rush is just six yards. One more thing. Rutgers head coach Greg Schiano said after last week’s 31-0 loss to Nebraska that Surace played with three broken ribs. “I’ve always had a lot of respect for AJ,” Schiano said . “But today, the toughness that he showed. AJ played today with three broken ribs. So he was an emergency player.” Surace was listed as questionable on Wednesday’s and Thursday’s availability report, and he’s still the likeliest of Rutgers’ three quarterbacks to play. Dylan Lonergan , who opened the season as the Scarlet Knights’ starter, was listed as doubtful, and other backup Sean Ashenfelder was listed as out. Expect Surace to play very conservatively against the Nittany Lions. With a nasty rib injury and two other quarterbacks expected to be out, it would behoove Surace to not risk any further injury and go down if contact from the pass rush is imminent. item.title: Canucks Rundown: Trade Talk, Hronek’s Agent Snaps, Penalty Trouble
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Friday’s Canucks Rundown will go over the latest trade talk and the penalty trouble the team has gotten into. Trade Talk: More of What We Knew The Canucks were a hot topic of conversation over the last few days, as the DFO Insider Podcast and the 32 Thoughts Podcast dropped the latest rumblings. It was more of the same ideas that we have heard since the offseason. Pending unrestricted free agents like Drew O’Connor , Luke Schenn , and Filip Chytil could be on their way out at the trade deadline. Jake DeBrusk still has a few suitors, and the other veterans, Filip Hronek , Brock Boeser , and Elias Pettersson , all want to stay with the Canucks for now. Rick Dhaliwal reiterated that fact Friday on the “Halford & Brough” show In the coming days, we will have another full piece on trade talk discussing the secondary market beyond the top five trade assets . Look out for that. Hronek’s Agent Fires Back Hronek’s agent, Allan Walsh, snapped back at the trade rumors. In a text to Rick Dhaliwal of CHEK’s “Donnie and Dhali”, Walsh wrote, “FULL NO MOVE. Waste of time. Waste of air. Clickbait for people with nothing better to do with their lives”. Obviously, Walsh is protecting his client here, and all reports point to the fact that Hronek has no intention of waiving his no-movement clause. Of course, that could always change later on, but at this point, no one has asked out of the Canucks. The Canucks defense corps would look like a mess if the Canucks traded Hronek away right now. Tom Willander would have to be on the top pairing. An important point was that Hronek is averaging nearly 27 minutes a game, while the third pair of right-shot defenders the Canucks have played are not getting much ice time at all. Cameron Crotty is averaging less than nine minutes per game, while Luke Schenn and Victor Mancini averaged around 12 and a half minutes. It says a lot about what the coaching staff thinks of their play. Trading Hronek should be a critical piece of business that the Canucks explore at some point, but judging from their current situation and how Manny Malhotra thinks of the third pairing right-shot defenders, it will not happen this season. item.description: The South Glens Falls girls' volleyball team poses for a photo after winning the Section 2 Class A championship over Glens Falls on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026 at Saratoga Springs High School. (Jess Koehler/For the Times Union) Alicia Collier is the Section 2 girls' volleyball coordinator. In that capacity, she spends a weekend in November every year in Glens Falls serving as the state tournament director at Harding Mazzotti Arena. Also the head coach for South Glens Falls, Collier has her players help out during the state tournament each year, too. This weekend, Collier and her Bulldogs are heading to Harding Mazzotti Arena in a different capacity - one of four teams competing in the Class A bracket. Earlier this month, South Glens Falls captured its first sectional title since winning the 2001 Class B title with a 3-1 decision over Foothills Council rival Glens Falls. South Glens Falls followed that up by defeating Massena in state regional play to earn a final four berth. "With the state tournament being in their back yard and with me being tournament director, these kids have worked and volunteered at this tournament because I have been involved since they were little kids," said Collier, who became the varsity coach at South Glens Falls in 2016. "They have been watching it and dreaming about being able to be an athlete on that floor. That, for me, is the coolest part: Getting to see these kids take in that experience. I am super excited for them." South Glens Falls defeated Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake in 2001 for the Class B sectional title. The following year, BH-BL beat South Glens Falls to start its streak of sectional championships that's now grown to 24 in a row. In all since 2002, BH-BL has beaten South Glens Falls eight times in sectional finals. Collier, whose team is one of five Section 2 programs to make it to the season's final weekend, is thrilled to be leading her squad into pool play on Saturday. The other three squads in the Class A field are Fulton (Section 3), Williamsville South (Section 6) and Plainedge (Section 8). "It is every coach's dream and every athlete's dream to win a championship. We've done so in our league a number of times, and that's awesome," Collier said. "So to get over the hump and win a sectional championship, then win a regional championship to get to the final four, is a big deal." "I think we will have a pretty big student section," said South Glens Falls senior setter Grace Smith, who has delivered 296 assists and 187 digs this season for the Bulldogs. "I have had a lot of teachers come up to me and tell me, 'Congratulations.' Some of them said they were going to be there on Saturday to watch." South Glens Falls captured the Foothills Council title and entered sectionals as the top seed. item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Just weeks after the NFL legend walked away from Birmingham City in what seemed like a messy parting of ways, Tom Brady has reportedly found himself a new club, and this time it’s one of the biggest names in the Premier League. He arrived promising to bring a winning culture to the second-tier English club. Things got off to a rough start. Brady later questioned Rooney’s work ethic in the Amazon docuseries Built in Birmingham: Brady & the Blues , and Rooney fired back by saying Brady “didn’t really understand football that well at that time.” Birmingham City announced Brady’s departure earlier this month, thanking him for his “unwavering support” over the last three years. But a source who spoke with Page Six painted a much different picture, claiming Brady had stopped showing up for the club long before he left. “He used to always support. He would go to games and support on social, and do press for their season,” the source said, before adding that eventually, “he completely checked out.” “He’d fly to NYC and walk in a Gucci runway show for $180,000, but wouldn’t go to BCFC games. item.description: Conte: ‘I would love to join an organised club, rather than always adding value’ Antonio Conte insists he would love ‘before ending my career to take over a club that is already organised’ after years of ‘building value’ from troubled situations like Juventus, Chelsea, Inter and Napoli. The coach is currently between jobs after walking away from Napoli in two years where he won the Serie A title and the Supercoppa Italiana. There were reports he could come to Manchester United or even return to his old side Juve, but he is in no rush for his next role. It never happened in my career, but evidently that is just the way it goes for me. I always arrived at complicated situations and was fortunate, but also deserve credit, for taking a team back to victory. “Often, it involved returning them to their history, a dimension that perhaps they had forgotten.” It all sounds like the scenario at Manchester United, who have not won the Premier League since 2013, following in the footsteps of other clubs he went through. item.title: Nick Saban reveals how view of ‘traditional’ blue-blood jobs has changed in NIL era
item.description: As the college football regular season winds down, the coaching carousel is starting to spin. Some notable jobs are in the spotlight, including Florida State after the firing of Mike Norvell earlier this month. But in the NIL and transfer portal era, the view of traditional blue-blood jobs has changed, according to former Alabama coach Nick Saban . Now, resources are the name of the game when it comes to building rosters – but that’s just one part of the equation. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “I think the ‘traditional’ really good jobs are no longer the best jobs,” Saban said Friday on The Pat McAfee Show . “And I think the way you look at a job is completely different than the way you would’ve done five years ago, 10 years ago. “Because now, it’s all about what kind of resources do we have to build a squad. Now, on the other side of that is because people can transfer, how many players could you bring with you if you went someplace else to turn a program around quickly?” Saban specifically cited the turnarounds at UCLA and Indiana . Bob Chesney has the Bruins undefeated entering Week 12 while Curt Cignetti took the Hoosiers from the losingest program in college football history to national champions in just two years. Both coaches came from James Madison and had key players re-join them at their new stops. Saban said that, along with having the proper resources, impacts the discussion around some of college football’s top jobs. “I think the dynamic is completely different,” Saban said. “If you don’t think you have the resources to sustain success where you are right now – and resources is about money right now, paying players. That’s what it comes down to. Then, maybe you’re better off taking a job where you do have the resources.” “If you think you have the resources, continuity is something that’s probably a little easier to build on if you do have the resources to continue to be able to grow your squad. Because your squad’s going to change every year.” The approach to roster-building is also important. In the era of player movement, backups could opt to enter the transfer portal and seek starting roles. That’s why coaches have to decide how to build the entire roster. “And then, what’s your philosophy of building your squad?” Nick Saban said. “How many significant players do you get, how many backup players do you lose, how many guys can you bring in for cheap that’ll take the place of those backup players? “So it’s building your squad from top to bottom, your roster. Some guys can do that pretty well. Some guys might struggle with it.”

item.title: Formula 1 set for V8 turbo return in 2030
item.description: Motorsport photo Formula 1 has moved closer to a return to V8 engines from the 2030 season as the FIA announced that a unanimous agreement has been reached between the governing body, F1 management and the power unit manufacturers. F1 has long worked towards cheaper and simpler engines for the next regulation cycle, which starts in 2031, having recognised the current formula is too complex and physically heavy, and a relic of a different direction in the road car industry. The FIA could have set the series’ future power-unit regulations for 2031, when the current cycle ends, but there has been broad alignment within the sport to bring that timeline forward by one year, driven by both president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali. So following recent gatherings by the F1 Commission and power unit advisory committee, where key aspects like the formula, timelines and costs were discussed, there had been broad support to bring forward the next generation of engine regulations by one year and curtail the current formula. The consensus is for F1 to move to a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 engine with a smaller electric component of 200kW, half of which will be ringfenced for overtake-mode use. The 2.1-litre capacity is derived from the current 1.6-litre V6 formula as a starting point, with two additional cylinders intended to reduce development costs. After an aborted announcement on Tuesday, the FIA has now officially confirmed there is unanimous support among its stakeholders about bringing that move forward to 2030. "The FIA presented F1 Power Unit regulations for introduction from 2030 with a 2.1 litre turbocharged V8 as the power unit of choice carrying over some geometrical specifics," the governing body said on Friday. "The overriding objective is to deliver a power unit which is a lot less complex, lighter and cheaper than the current power units. It will feature limited hybridisation, relevant and sustainable technology with the aim of enhancing attack-oriented racing and a sound which resonates with fans. "Additionally, the plan is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing. " F1 and FIA F1 and FIA Ben Sulayem added: "This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1. “From the outset I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. "The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide. “Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition." item.title: Leeds United receive double injury boost ahead of Chelsea clash
item.description: Leeds United receive double injury boost ahead of Chelsea clash Leeds Handed Anton Stach Boost Ahead of Chelsea Clash at Stamford Bridge Leeds United head to Stamford Bridge with a useful bit of news for Daniel Farke. Anton Stach is expected to be back in the squad, and that matters. He has been one of Leeds’ more reliable performers since arriving last summer, giving them presence, control and a level of consistency that has been hard to ignore. Stach missed the home defeat to Tottenham after suffering a broken toe, but the signs now point firmly towards a return. Farke made it clear the midfielder has come through an important week on the training pitch and is back in the frame for Saturday’s trip to Chelsea. “He [Stach] was a full week back in training, today,” Farke explained at his pre-match press conference. “Last week, still a bit like part integrated and a bit of individual rehab work.” Anton Stach Return Lifts Leeds United That is the headline for Leeds. Stach’s recovery gives Farke another serious option in midfield, and it arrives at the right time. Leeds need ballast away at Chelsea, especially against a side still capable of controlling games even while results have wobbled. Farke also offered positive updates on Noah Okafor and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. “Both of them had a full training week and it was definitely beneficial. “Dominic [Calvert-Lewin], since he came back from England duties, is also back in training and no problems, so definitely good news.” Photo IMAGO Put simply, Leeds are close to full strength. For a difficult away fixture, that is no small thing. Chelsea Injuries Add Uncertainty Chelsea’s recent league form has lacked stability. One win in the last three tells its own story, with defeats to Sunderland and Tottenham either side of a 2-0 victory over Manchester United. They are still dangerous, but they are hardly in cruise control. Xabi Alonso also has fitness concerns to manage. Joao Pedro remains a doubt, Moises Caicedo has returned from international duty with an issue, while Reece James is recovering from knee surgery. Maxence Lacroix is also sidelined until the new year. Stamford Bridge Test Looks More Balanced On paper, Chelsea still have the stronger squad. In reality, this looks tighter than that. Leeds arrive healthier, more settled and with Anton Stach potentially back in the mix. That gives Farke a fighting chance of making this awkward for the hosts.

item.description: The Indianapolis Colts will carry nearly $15 million in dead money for Daniel Jones this season if the veteran quarterback clears waivers, capping a collapse that turned a two-year, $88 million commitment into one of the NFL ’s costliest misfires. Head coach Shane Steichen announced the move Friday, and Jones’ projected dead cap charge lands at $14,889,520 for 2026 and $35.2 million for 2027 if no team claims him off waivers. That brings Indianapolis’ total spend to $49.8 million for 11 starts. Jones sits on waivers until Monday at 4 p.m. ET. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
